page_title: Mount ext4 Linux USB drives, HDDs, or SSDs on macOS | ExtendFS

sources.entry: ExtendFS - Read-only access to Linux ext2/3/4 in macOS Sequoia and later without a kernel extension. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/kthchew/ExtendFS) [![App Store][app-store Icon]](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/mount-ext4-drives-extendfs/id6755664332?platform=mac)

summary.name: ExtendFS
summary.one_liner: A read-only ext2/ext3/ext4 file system driver for macOS that uses Apple's FSKit framework so Linux-formatted drives mount without a kernel extension or terminal.
use_cases: Read files from an ext4 USB drive plugged into a Mac
Access an SD card used with a Raspberry Pi on macOS
Browse a Linux PC's external hard drive in Finder
Mount ext4 disk images on a Mac
Pull files off a NAS drive on macOS
summary.what_it_does: ExtendFS is a read-only driver for ext2, ext3, and ext4 file systems on macOS, written in Swift and built on Apple's FSKit framework. Once the app is run and its file system extension is enabled in System Settings, supported ext4 volumes mount automatically and appear in Finder when plugged in or when a disk image is opened. It can also be mounted from the command line using mount -t ExtendFS. The filesystem runs in user space and is sandboxed, without FUSE or a kernel extension. The source code is on GitHub under GPL.
notable: Uses FSKit instead of FUSE or a kernel extension, so no reboot into recovery mode is needed
Sandboxed, signed and notarized; works with macOS Full Security mode
Open source under GPL; Mac App Store version has no differences from the free source build
Automatic mounting in Finder with no terminal required
caveats: Read-only: no write access to ext4 volumes
Does not support ext4 compression, encryption, meta block groups, or LVM
Requires macOS 15.6 or later; Btrfs and other file systems are not supported
